speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (a) whether there has been a significant rise in the average cost of living for Singaporeans since 2010 in terms of basic necessities/staple food, transportation, housing and medical care relative to other major cities with and without the same standard of living and full accessibility of goods and services respectively; and (b) how will the Government continue to provide Singaporeans with a higher standard of living and maintaining a lower cost of living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: The Consumer Price Index can be used as a proxy for changes in the cost of living in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: However, most of the inflation over this period occurred in the earlier years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: The Member asked about the inflation experience of other major cities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: As most national statistical offices do not publish inflation data at the city level, we will look at the experiences of the three Newly Industrialised Economies (NIEs) of Hong Kong, South Korea and Taiwan instead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: Apart from looking at the cost of living, we should also consider households' income growth which affects their ability to meet these costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: Between 2010 and 2017, resident households’ incomes increased faster than the inflation rate, leading to positive real income growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: Nonetheless, the Government recognises that cost of living may be of concern for some groups, particularly retirees and lower income households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: The Government provides significant support for Singaporeans, such as in pre-school, education, housing, healthcare and public transport, to ensure that these are affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: For needy families who require more support due to their unique circumstances, additional help is available at our Social Service Offices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
text: This will, in turn, help to ensure a higher standard of living for Singaporeans.
